items.title: Pochettino’s new-manager bounce falls flat with De Ligt move a disastrous step | Jamie Jackson
items.summary: Decision to pick the Dutch defender over Harry Maguire backfired as Manchester United fell apart in the Anfield bearpit Chaotic, bewildering, and on this evidence in a relegation dogfight: welcome to the three‑ring circus that is Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino. This ended as a 4-0 rout in favour of Liverpool, the new head coach overseeing the poorest opening result of the eight who have followed Sir Alex Ferguson since May 2013. Factor in this result coming against United’s fiercest rivals and Pochettino’s despair is complete.

Fernandes’s current deal expires at the end of this campaign, although United ⁠hold an ​option to extend their captain’s contract by a further year until June 2028, giving the club more time to reach ⁠an agreement on fresh terms.

items.title: ‘Obviously it’s not good’: Arteta sweating over David Raya’s fitness after injury
items.summary: Keeper close to tears at Newcastle after hurting shoulder Arsenal held 2-2, with Jaissle hailing ‘excellent’ display Arsenal were left sweating on the fitness of their goalkeeper David Raya after the Spaniard was forced off with a shoulder injury during the second half of the 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday evening. It left Mikel Arteta’s side six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City at the top of the Premier League but Arsenal’s manager was more concerned about Raya following an accidental collision with Newcastle’s William Osula. The Spaniard was helped off in evident pain and looked close to tears.

items.title: European football: Doué carried off for PSG while Kane vows to return fresh
items.summary: Doué injury adds to that of Kvaratskhelia last month Nice 2-3 PSG; Lazio 3-0 Lecce; Gladbach 0-1 Dortmund Désiré Doué was carried off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as Paris Saint-Germain beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1. Doué went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. The match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doué to receive treatment to his right knee before he was carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium.

items.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet
items.summary: The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality. He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym.

items.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
items.summary: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans.
